post_understanding.summary: A T-SQL query that joins Always On Availability Groups DMVs to list secondary replicas is taking ~12m38s to return 34 rows on a primary replica. Execution plan shows internal DMVs/TVFs calling cluster APIs, and waits are HADR_CLUSAPI_CALL. Environment has ~53 Availability Groups across multiple subnets; refreshing the AG tree in SSMS is also slow. Materializing sys.availability_groups and sys.availability_replicas into temp tables reduced runtime to ~1m03s.
symptoms: very slow metadata query (~12m38s) returning only 34 rows
IO and CPU minimal while elapsed time is very high
SSMS Availability Groups node refresh is slow
suspected_root_causes: real-time cluster API enumeration by HADR DMVs scaling poorly with many Availability Groups
cross-subnet network latency inflating cluster API call time
optimizer timeout and repeated re-enumeration of DMVs during joins
key_evidence: Execution plan shows internal TVFs like DM_HADR_INTERNAL_* and StatementOptmEarlyAbortReason='TimeOut'.
Statistics IO shows small reads; CPU time 1266 ms vs elapsed 747,852 ms.
Materializing sys.availability_groups and sys.availability_replicas into temp tables speeds run to ~1m03s.
assumptions: SQL Server version is 2014 (12.0.2370.0) or similar, running on Windows Server Failover Cluster with Always On enabled.
Topology consists of 3 nodes (1 primary, 2 secondary replicas) across at least two subnets/sites.
Roughly 50+ Availability Groups exist, each with at least one database.
Network latency between subnets is non-trivial (e.g., 50–150 ms RTT), contributing to HADR_CLUSAPI_CALL waits.
The query is executed on the primary replica and not on a read-only secondary.
No heavy foreground workload; slowness is dominated by external cluster API calls rather than database contention.
Security context has permissions to query the DMVs involved.

background_workloads.name: AG metadata polling query
background_workloads.inferred_from_post: The post runs a DMV-heavy SELECT that joins AG metadata to list secondaries; it is the primary workload causing waits.
transactions_or_queries: SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL READ UNCOMMITTED; SET STATISTICS TIME, IO ON;
SELECT ISNULL(agstates.primary_replica, '') AS Primary_AG_Server, dbcs.database_name, ar.replica_server_name
LEFT JOIN sys.dm_hadr_availability_group_states AS agstates ON AG.group_id = agstates.group_id
INNER JOIN sys.availability_replicas AS AR ON AG.group_id = AR.group_id
INNER JOIN sys.dm_hadr_availability_replica_states AS arstates ON AR.replica_id = arstates.replica_id AND arstates.is_local <> 1
INNER JOIN sys.dm_hadr_database_replica_cluster_states AS dbcs ON arstates.replica_id = dbcs.replica_id

anomaly_injection.name: Create many Availability Groups
anomaly_injection.method: Provision a large number of small AGs with one tiny database each across 3 nodes (1 primary, 2 secondaries).

parameters.commit_mode: mix of synchronous and asynchronous acceptable

safety_notes: Creating dozens of AGs consumes WSFC and SQL resources; only run in an isolated lab.
Ensure automatic seeding or small databases to avoid long data synchronization times.

anomaly_injection.name: Cross-subnet network latency
anomaly_injection.method: Introduce controlled latency between AG nodes using a network emulator in the virtualization platform or OS-level network emulation.
safety_notes: Do not apply to production; network impairment can affect AG health and failover.
Set health-check timeouts appropriately to avoid unintended failovers in lab.

anomaly_injection.name: Baseline query vs. temp table optimization
anomaly_injection.method: Run the baseline DMV join query, then run variant that preloads sys.availability_groups and sys.availability_replicas into temp tables before the join.
safety_notes: Use READ UNCOMMITTED as in the post to match behavior.

query_or_transaction_effects: Baseline DMV query takes multiple minutes to return a few dozen rows.
Execution plan shows internal TVFs (DM_HADR_INTERNAL_*) and optimizer timeout.
After materializing sys.availability_groups and sys.availability_replicas into temp tables, runtime significantly decreases (e.g., to ~1 minute or less).
validation_criteria: During baseline run, sys.dm_exec_requests shows wait_type = HADR_CLUSAPI_CALL for the query for a substantial portion of elapsed time.
SET STATISTICS TIME, IO shows CPU time in low seconds while elapsed time is high (> 600s) and reads are modest.
Returned row count in the tens (e.g., ~34) consistent with secondary replicas across AGs and filter is_local <> 1.
Plan includes DM_HADR_INTERNAL_* TVFs and StatementOptmEarlyAbortReason='TimeOut'.
Temp table variant measurably reduces elapsed time versus baseline on the same environment.

Is the query executed on the primary or a secondary replica, and is the secondary readable intent enabled?
